records.name: Community Gardens Network (Farm Philly)
records.summary: The city's network of 19 community gardens on park land, where about 500 residents grow food together. Farm Philly provides land access, compost, mulch, supplies, workshops, and training.
records.what_you_do: Grow food in a shared garden alongside neighbors, and take part in the workshops and training Farm Philly offers growers.

schedule.text: Set by each garden. Find a garden on the city's map or email farmphilly@phila.gov.

cost.text: The city page does not list garden fees.

first_step.how: Find a registered garden on the city's map and contact it, or email farmphilly@phila.gov.
first_step.basis: The city page gives a clear way to find a garden and contact it, and says Farm Philly runs workshops and training for growers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each garden is a shared growing space on Parks and Recreation land, and about 500 neighbors grow food together across 19 sites. Farm Philly supplies land access, compost, mulch, wood chips, and supplies, and its staff teach workshops. The city page does not say what a garden charges or when members meet, so ask the garden you contact.
first_visit_tips: Contact the garden before you visit, since the city page does not list visiting hours.
Ask about fees, plot rules, and how new members join.
Ask Farm Philly about workshops if you are new to growing food.

records.notes: Garden count (19) and grower count (about 500) come from the city gardening page. The phone number is the Farm Philly program line on the program page. Fees, plot rules, visiting hours, and accessibility are not stated by the city, and the city garden map could not be read as text. Status stays probably_active because no dated item was found.

records.name: Community Schools Special Projects
records.summary: Community Schools Special Projects lists one time and short term volunteer projects at the City's Community Schools, posted on the City's volunteer portal.
records.what_you_do: Help with school based programs for students and families.

first_step.how: Email commschools@phila.gov or call 215-683-6012 and ask how to sign up for a volunteer project.
first_step.basis: The city lists a public phone line and email, but its page does not say how volunteers sign up, and the project listing could not be reopened today.
first_step.what_to_expect: The city's pages do not describe what a volunteer day looks like. Ask the Community Schools office what a specific project involves, where it happens, and how long it lasts before you commit.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the school, the address, and the start time before you go.
Ask whether the project needs a background check or clearance.

records.notes: The city volunteer portal listing returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch today, so the project list, sign-up steps, and any clearance rules are not verified. Name, website, and the project summary are carried from the tier 1 read. The city's main page shows a May 2026 post and October 2026 upcoming events, which give the sign of life. The city page lists 20 Community Schools serving nearly 13,000 students but does not describe volunteer sign-up.

records.name: Compass Pro Bono (Philadelphia)
records.summary: Connects Philadelphia nonprofits with business professionals. Volunteers can join a consulting team for four to eight months, guide a nonprofit leader for eight weeks, or serve on a nonprofit board after training.
records.what_you_do: Join a team on a consulting project (a few hours a week), guide a nonprofit leader for eight weeks, or serve on a nonprofit board after training.

first_step.how: Register for a general information session listed on the Compass Philadelphia page, or create an account on the volunteer portal to apply.
first_step.basis: Volunteers apply through a portal and are matched. Public information sessions are listed, but the page does not say what the application or matching involves.
first_step.what_to_expect: Consulting work takes a few hours a week, and team projects run four or eight months. One-on-one guidance runs eight weeks. Board members receive training, but the page does not say how long it runs or what it costs, and it does not say what the application asks or whether there is a fee.
first_visit_tips: Attend an information session first, since the page lists several with registration links.
Ask about training length and the hours a board seat takes before you apply, since the page does not give them.

records.notes: Dated items are season only (Summer 2026 for a celebration and a summit, Winter and Spring 2025 for a happy hour) or have no year (information sessions on October 15, October 28, and November 12, and a webinar on October 16). Status therefore stays probably_active instead of active. Fees, training length, and application questions are not stated. The volunteer portal link was taken from the page, not opened.

records.name: Cradle of Liberty Council, Scouting America
records.summary: The Scouting America council for Philadelphia, Montgomery and Delaware Counties. It runs Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, Venturing, Sea Scouts and Exploring through local units, and it checks the adults who lead them first.
records.what_you_do: Youth join a local unit by age: Cub Scouts for ages 5 to 10, Scouts BSA for ages 11 to 17, Venturing and Sea Scouts for ages 14 to 20, and Exploring for ages 10 to 20. Adults can take unit roles such as Scoutmaster, Cubmaster or committee member, after youth safety training and Pennsylvania clearances, with an online application at beascout.org that carries a fee.

schedule.text: Each unit sets its own meeting times, and the council's pages do not list them.

locations.label: Service Center
locations.address: 901 East 8th Ave, Suite 103, King of Prussia, PA 19406

cost.text: The council pages do not state a youth membership fee. Adult volunteer applications carry a registration fee, and the amount is not stated.

first_step.how: Find a program near you at beascout.scouting.org, or call the service center at 610-688-6900 to ask which unit is closest.
first_step.basis: Families get a clear route to a unit and a phone line to ask. Adult leaders finish safeguarding training and Pennsylvania clearances before they take a role, which takes time before a first visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each unit sets its own meeting times, so the first visit depends on the unit you contact. For adult leaders, the first steps are safeguarding training, Pennsylvania clearances, and a registration application with a fee. Clearances are free for most volunteers and valid for five years.
first_visit_tips: Call 610-688-6900 to ask which unit is closest to you before you go.
For an adult role, fingerprints are required unless you have lived in Pennsylvania for 10 or more consecutive years.
Save your safeguarding training certificate as a PDF, since you need its Scouting America ID number later.

records.notes: The clearance and background check flags apply to adult leader roles only. Youth need no clearance stated on the pages. Youth age ranges come from the council's programs page: Cub Scouts 5 to 10, Scouts BSA 11 to 17, Venturing and Sea Scouts 14 to 20, Exploring 10 to 20. The events page shows a 2026 to 2027 membership notice and a note that names 2025 qualifiers, but neither has a month, so status stays probably_active. The Labor Day notice and the Celebration of Scouting date carry no year and are not used. No family join night is listed. Youth fee and adult fee amount are not stated.

records.name: Cranaleith Spiritual Center
records.summary: Volunteers help care for the ten acre grounds of a spiritual center in Northeast Philadelphia, from the vegetable garden and bees to the labyrinth and visitor welcome.
records.what_you_do: Work the vegetable garden, adopt a garden or tree, help bottle honey, do lawn and grounds work, greet visitors, decorate for holidays, or help at events.

first_step.how: Send the volunteer form from the Join Our Team button on the volunteer page, or call or email the center to say what kind of help you would like.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page welcomes individuals and groups of all ages and skill levels and gives a clear form, but it does not describe an orientation or a set schedule.
first_step.what_to_expect: The page lists garden, grounds, bee, greeter, and event jobs, and asks you to say how you would like to help. It does not say how long a shift lasts, whether there is an orientation, or what to wear, so ask when you make contact.
first_visit_tips: Tell the center the kind of job you want, such as the garden, the greeter desk, or events.
Ask about parking when you call, since the center's site says free onsite parking is offered for its conference center.

records.notes: The Join Our Team button opens a volunteer form hosted on retreat.guru, not on the center's own site. The volunteer page has no orientation, schedule, what-to-wear, or background check details. The events page lists past events and blog posts with no scheduled volunteer days. Grounds or labyrinth visiting hours, accessibility, and any visitor fees are not stated. The /about/ and /visit/ pages returned 404. The labyrinth appears in the volunteer job list. Last sign of life is the July 25, 2026 blog post on the events page.

records.name: CultureWorks Greater Philadelphia
records.summary: A Center City nonprofit that handles the paperwork for more than 90 creative projects and rents affordable desk space to cultural workers.
records.what_you_do: Take a writing course, attend a networking or professional development event for cultural leaders, rent a desk in the coworking space, or apply to have your project fiscally sponsored.

schedule.text: Networking events, workshops, and multi-week courses are posted on the events page. No weekly schedule is published.

cost.text: Some events are free, such as the Connect and Dream Together networking event. Most listings do not give a price, and desk membership prices are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Pick a networking event or course on the events page and RSVP, or email info@cultureworksphila.org with questions.
first_step.basis: Events are listed publicly and some are free, but most listed events need an RSVP or registration. Desk space needs membership and fiscal sponsorship needs an application.
first_step.what_to_expect: Networking events and mixers bring cultural workers together at CultureWorks on Walnut Street, and some mixers serve light bites and drinks. Courses run for several weeks and need registration ahead of time. Most listings do not state a price, so check the event page before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Check whether the event is in person (Suite 300 or Suite 320) or on Zoom, since the listings name both.
Register early, because courses close when they fill.
Ask about the price before you register, since most listings do not give one.

records.notes: Writing categories were added because the events page lists two multi-week writing courses (Tackling NaNoWriMo Together and Poetry as Resistance). The events page prints 2026 next to its October dates, which supports last_sign_of_life 2026-10. The Cocusocial cooking classes held in the building are run by another group and are listed as a lead. The /coworking/ link redirects to /membership, which returned 404, so desk prices, eligibility, and fiscal sponsorship fees remain unknown. Some events use Suite 320, not Suite 300, so the location lists the building address.

records.name: Curio Theatre Company
records.summary: A professional theater company in West Philadelphia that has been staging plays since 2005. It also runs CuriosiTeens!, a free company for local teens.
records.what_you_do: Teens aged 13 to 17 can join CuriosiTeens! for free and learn theater on Saturday mornings. Adults can see the season, look at the subscription packages, join the mailing list, or give to the spotlight fund.

schedule.text: CuriosiTeens! meets Saturdays, 10 am to noon.

locations.label: Calvary Center for Culture and Community (side door on 48th Street)

cost.text: CuriosiTeens! is free. Show ticket prices are not listed on the site.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: the 34 trolley, with the stop at the corner of Baltimore Avenue and South 48th Street, per the theater's directions page. For elevator access at the theater, call or email ahead.

first_step.how: Call 215-921-8243, or use the Contact Us page on the site, to ask about joining a Saturday session for teens aged 13 to 17.
first_step.basis: The teen company is free and open to local teens who call or write. The page describes no audition or formal application.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each Saturday session runs 10 am to noon at the Calvary Center on Baltimore Avenue. Teens play theater games, learn how a play is built, and help choose, cast, design, and build a show that the company performs for the community. There is no cost to take part.
first_visit_tips: Enter by the side door on 48th Street at 4740 Baltimore Avenue.
Take the SEPTA 34 trolley to the corner of Baltimore Avenue and 48th Street, or drive and look for the free Parking Authority lot at 4716 to 4723 Baltimore Avenue (spaces depend on availability).
Call ahead to confirm when the next session starts, since the page does not list what to bring or wear.

records.notes: The 2026 season (Season 22, 2026 to 2027) and the 2026 production are named, but no month or ticket price is printed, so status stays probably_active and no last_sign_of_life is written. The season length (season field) is left out because the pages do not say whether teen sessions run all year. The teen page gives the 48th Street side door at the Calvary Center for teen sessions, while the theater directions page describes a Baltimore Avenue entrance for the theater itself, so check which door to use. The teen page says 12-year-olds may be accepted case by case, so min_age is 13 as stated. The teen page also lists a June 2024 production that may be out of date. The email address on the teen page is hidden, so the phone and Contact Us page are the recorded routes.
